//: Allowlist for the shipped-examples execution gate (shipped-examples-execution.test.ts).
Each entry is a shipped handler whose DOM effect DIVERGES between hyperfixi and the
real hyperscript.org engine when its trigger event is dispatched in jsdom.
Keys embed a hash of the source: editing the handler changes the key, so entries go
stale and the stale-entry assertion forces their removal — the list only ratchets down.

2026-08-31 — recipes.html::keyup REMOVED, and this is a coverage LOSS worth stating rather than a convergence. The parser now reports the input it discards, and that handler is one of the sources it reports on, so this gate's eligibility filter ('hyperfixi does not compile it clean') now skips it. Its recorded reason here was ALSO A MISDIAGNOSIS: not a show/hide-strategy difference, but hyperfixi silently discarding the `in the next <div/> when its textContent contains my value` clause — so it showed every blockquote where upstream filtered. Upstream ACCEPTS that source, so it is a real hyperfixi parser defect; it is now tracked by the shipped-sources validity gate instead, and it comes back here the moment the parse is fixed.

2026-10-01 — the four swap-morph.html `swap afterBegin/beforeEnd of X with Y` entries REMOVED: the page now writes `put Y at start of / at end of X`, which both engines run to the same DOM. (The old reason, 'upstream has no swap command, so it no-ops', was half right: upstream's `swap a with b` exchanges two values, so the source set an expando property and inserted nothing.) Two `toggle *display of X` entries ADDED, a new bookkeeping family: see their reason.

2026-10-01 — ENGINE LANE added: `allowedEngineDivergences` lists the handlers whose effect on @hyperfixi/engine differs from upstream's. First run: 134 compared, 89 real matches, 44 empty on both, 1 diverging, and that one is upstream's stale `document` in this harness. (The core lane over the same handlers: 31 diverging.)

2026-10-02 — the thirteen `increment #x` / `decrement #x` entries REMOVED: the pages now write `increment #x's textContent`, which hyperfixi, upstream and @hyperfixi/engine run to the same DOM (core counted in the element's text; upstream and the engine do not, and the element was gone after one click). The rewrite uncovered what those entries hid on counter.html: its mirror handler, `on change in #count`, a second core-only reading (upstream reads `in` as a filter on where the event came from). The mirror now writes upstream's `on mutation of childList from #count`, and the page loads hyperfixi-hs.js.

2026-10-02 — the three multilingual/showcase.html tab entries REMOVED: the handlers ended `hide .tab-panel then show #panelN`, and the panels are hidden by a stylesheet rule, which upstream's `show` does not override (it clears the inline display; core sets one). They now switch the `.active` class the stylesheet already keys on, which both engines run to the same DOM; the page loads hyperfixi-hs.js.

allowedDivergences.reason: show/hide strategy: hyperfixi uses class + inline display; upstream consults computed styles and is inert under jsdom. The marker CLASS is the whole remaining divergence here — the shipped input is empty, so `contains ""` holds for every blockquote and both engines show all four; upstream's show is a no-op on an already-visible element, hyperfixi's adds `.show`. The FILTER itself was measured against upstream with real search terms (a run with the input pre-filled, which this gate cannot do — it dispatches the page as shipped): for `code`, `zzz` and `programmer` the two engines produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL hide set, and the only diff is `.show` on the elements hyperfixi shows. Returned to this gate by the show/hide parser fix; before it this handler was skipped as 'hyperfixi does not compile it clean'.
